overview: This one-page file consists of a Department of State list-of-papers sheet recording a Tokyo telegram concerning labor and immigration conditions in Formosa (Taiwan). The entry describes rules governing the temporary admission and residence of foreign instrumentalists, other musicians and artists, actors, choristers, and other aliens seeking employment, and indicates that a copy of the relevant rules and regulations was enclosed. The telegram itself is not present here; the sheet directs the reader to file 894a.55/4.

subfiles.title: List of papers entry for Tokyo telegram No. 943 on alien performers in Formosa
subfiles.about: The sheet records and cross-references a Tokyo telegram on rules governing the temporary admission, residence, and employment of foreign performers and other aliens in Formosa.
subfiles.summary: This Department of State list-of-papers sheet describes Tokyo telegram No. 943, associated with Garrels and dated November 17. The telegram concerned labor conditions in Formosa, particularly the temporary admission and residence of instrumental musicians, other musicians and artists, actors, choristers, and other aliens for employment. It reportedly enclosed a copy of the applicable rules and regulations. The entry directs the reader to decimal file 894a.55/4, where the substantive document was apparently filed.

interest: The sheet is useful chiefly as a provenance and cross-filing record: it identifies a substantive telegram that is absent from this bundle and points historians to its likely location in another decimal-file category. Its wording also reveals that colonial Taiwan maintained specific admission, residence, and employment rules for foreign entertainers and other alien workers, offering a lead for research into labor control, migration, and cultural performance under Japanese rule.
